title: Influence of the menstrual cycle on anaerobic performance, pain perception, and muscle and tendon stiffness
summary:
This study investigates whether athletic performance, pain perception, and biomechanical properties of muscles and tendons change across the menstrual cycle. Hormonal fluctuations during the cycle may influence how women perform during intense physical exercise and how their bodies respond to such loads. The aim of the study is therefore to determine whether anaerobic performance, pain sensitivity, and the stiffness of muscles and tendons differ between different phases of the menstrual cycle.
25 healthy young are eligible to participate in the study. In addition, a comparison group of 25 male participants will be included. All participants will first undergo a medical screening examination including an exercise test on a cycle ergometer.
Subsequently, female participants will attend two additional testing sessions scheduled during different phases of the menstrual cycle (early follicular phase and mid-luteal phase). During each session, participants will perform an intensive 90-second cycling exercise on a cycle ergometer. Before and after the exercise, pain sensitivity and the stiffness of muscles and tendons will be assessed using standardized measurement procedures. In addition, a venous blood sample will be taken from the female participants to determine hormone levels. Male participants will complete only one additional testing session without blood sampling.
The results of this study are expected to improve the understanding of the influence of the menstrual cycle on athletic performance, exercise-induced pain processing, and exercise-induced changes in the biomechanical properties of muscles and tendons. Ultimately, the findings may contribute to improved training strategies and sports medicine care tailored to women.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- for women: documented regular menstrual cycle (21–35 days) during the past 3 months.
Exclusion criteria:
- for women: pregnancy
- for women: hormonal contraception
- for women: absent or irregular menstrual cycle
- chronic pain
- current injuries or illnesses
- diagnosed chronic diseases (e.g., hypertension, diabetes)
- regular use of pain medication
